paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus doesn't wait for His followers to get their faith together before He uses them. They were mourning and weeping. They did not believe Mary, and they did not believe the two from the country either. Then Jesus appeared to the Eleven and rebuked them for their "unbelief and hardness of heart" (Mark 16:14), and in the very next breath He handed them the whole world as their job.

That tells you something about Him, and it should make you breathe easy. He knew exactly who He was sending. Mary had seven demons driven out of her (Mark 16:9), and she was the first one He appeared to. If anybody ever told you that you're too doubtful, too messy or too worn out to be useful, I've got news. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer before the Most High called me out, so I'm living proof He picks the ones nobody else would.

And look at how it ends. Jesus is taken up into heaven and sits down at the right hand of God (Mark 16:19). Then the same Eleven who wouldn't believe the news "went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked through them" (Mark 16:20). They weren't left on their own. So when He sends you, baker, you're not carrying it alone either. This is the end of this story, but He is still working through people who believe, and I'm keeping my ovens ready.
